claims.text: Some passages announce pardon, while others answer through comfort, peace, rebuke, intercession, or no narrated resolution.
The sources distinguish pardon from restitution, wilderness sentence, vengeance for deeds, sufficient punishment, comfort, and restored communal love.

Prayer teaching, apostolic proclamation, household reception, and community testing relate forgiveness to materially different actions and orders.
The sources place forgiveness within legal rites, intercession, meal speech, sanctuary argument, and advocacy while preserving each action and literary frame.
Poetry, reconciliation, cross imagery, and covenant argument use different language for guilt, charge, memory, and restored relation.
